newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-Brazil's Coelba fetches big premium.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Brazil's Coelba fetches big premium.

text.p: Brazil's Bahia state on Thursday sold a controlling stake in power utility Coelba for 1.73 billion reais ($1.6 billion), making it the largest privatization ever by a state government there.

A consortium led by Spain's second-largest power utility, Iberdrola SA, placed the winning bid for the 65.64 percent voting stake in Coelba, or Companhia de Eletricidade do Estado da Bahia. The group also includes Brazil's largest pension fund Previ and Banco do Brasil's brokerage arm.
The winning bid was 77.38 percent above the minimum price of 975.8 million reais ($903.5 million), exceeding by far the market's expectations of a 30 to 40 percent premium.

"This is a new record in state privatizations," Jose Pio Borges, vice president of National Development Bank (BNDES), told reporters after the auction on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange. BNDES oversees Brazil's privatization process.
The sale ranks as Brazil's third-largest privatization overall, after Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) and electricity distributor Light, which were owned by the federal government.
"This was just a bombshell," said Charles Barnett, director of Latin American electricity sector research at ING Baring. "The market was way off in valuing this thing."
Iberdrola Director Eduardo Lopez-Aranguren Marcos said the consortium planned to invest $500 million in Coelba over the next five years, according to investment plans already drawn up by Coelba.

He said the money would be invested in power distribution and the group would await the creation of a definitive privatization model of Brazil's electricity sector before deciding whether to invest in power generation as well.
He said Coelba's new controlling shareholders had no plans to introduce any "radical" changes to the company or the size of its 4,700-strong workforce.
Iberdrola has a 40 percent share in power generation and distribution in Spain with production of 56,000 gigawatts per year, installed capacity of 16,000 megawatts and eight million customers.

Iberdrola also runs electricity and natural gas ventures in Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Colombia. Two weeks ago took part in a consortium that clinched the bids on two Rio de Janeiro state natural gas companies, CEG and Riogas.

Bahia state will receive 1.5 billion reais ($1.39 billion) from the Coelba sale with the remainder of the auction receipts going to BNDES and the federal power holding company, Centrais Eletricas Brasileiras SA, or Eletrobras, which owned some of the shares auctioned.

Bahia Gov. Paulo Souto said the state would invest privatization receipts in education, health, public security and the modernization of its infrastructure as well as in improving its fiscal performance.
Coelba's new controlling shareholders will have to pay the auction price in full in cash August 6, but BNDES is offering to finance 50 percent of the minimum price.
